cards.text: This psalm opens with "Hallelujah!" and goes straight to praise from the very first word. Me, I can't even get out a good morning until my third cookie. Then the psalm paints a picture of one kind of man and calls him blessed.

cards.question: Who is the man this psalm calls blessed?

answers.text: The man who fears the LORD
The man who leads an army
The man who builds a city

cards.question: When it comes to the LORD's commandments, the man who fears Him greatly ___.

cards.text: Now the psalm zooms out past this one man to his descendants, the WHOLE family tree. I've got six cookie cutter kids, friend, and I STILL can't stop bragging about them.

cards.question: True or false: The psalm says the descendants of the man who fears the LORD will be mighty in the land.

cards.text: Then the psalm walks into his house, and wealth and riches are in it. Me, I call it a rich day when I find a spare bag of chocolate chips behind the flour.

cards.question: True or false: The psalm says the righteousness of this man who fears the LORD endures forever.

cards.text: Next, the psalm heads into the darkness. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer with darkness as my roommate, and it never paid rent ONCE.

cards.question: The psalm says something comes for the upright, the gracious, compassionate and righteous, right there in the darkness. What is it?
The psalm says it is well with a certain kind of man. What is he like?

answers.text: He is generous and lends freely
He spends it all on himself
He keeps his money hidden away

cards.question: True or false: The psalm says the man whose affairs are guided by justice will one day be shaken.

cards.text: In fact, the righteous man will be remembered forever. Then the psalm brings up what every adult dreads: bad news, like your boss texting "Got a minute?" at eleven at night.

cards.question: The man who fears the LORD does not fear bad news. What does the psalm say about his heart?

answers.text: It is steadfast and trusting in the LORD
It is heavy and worried about tomorrow
It is set on keeping his riches safe

cards.text: The psalm says, "His heart is assured; he does not fear, until he looks in triumph on his foes." Me, I jump every time the oven timer dings, and I'm the one who SET it.

cards.question: This man doesn't keep his gifts to himself. He scatters them abroad to the ___.

cards.text: That line again: his righteousness endures forever. And his horn will be lifted high in honor.

cards.question: At the very end, the psalm turns to the wicked man and says he will see. How will the wicked man react?

answers.text: He will be grieved and gnash his teeth
He will change his ways and give
He will laugh and walk away

cards.text: He will waste away. And the psalm ends right there, quiet: the desires of the wicked will perish.
